self_check.method: k1623_rev3_selfcheck.py — regex rules over all claim-surface files, in Python.
self_check.why_not_grep: grep on this machine resolves to ugrep, where `-r` plus an explicit multi-file list degrades to 'No such file or directory' and then reports ZERO hits. An initial grep-based sweep produced 11 false 'no residual' results before this was caught. A checker that cannot fail is worse than no checker.
self_check.negative_control: Injecting three retracted claims into README.md (2.51e-3 / HAR 冠軍 / 所有數字不變) made three rules FAIL and the exit code flip to 1; reverting returned it to 0. The check demonstrably catches regressions.
checker_defects_found_and_fixed_during_t: grep/ugrep silent zero-hit — replaced with Python scanning of read bytes.

Marker `NOT ` was so loose that the frozen finding_3 passed on the strength of an unrelated 'not evidence of additional level shifts'. Marker list narrowed to phrases only used when retracting; that site now goes through the written allowlist instead.

JSON was allowed to borrow a retraction marker from the neighbouring line, which is how finding_3 was rescued by finding_4's 'IS NOT much inflated'. JSON is now judged one line at a time; only .py/.md use a window, where statements genuinely wrap.

The pattern was compiled without re.I, so 'Break DATES are estimated with substantial uncertainty' (capital B) — the exact sentence B4c retracts — was never scanned at all, and the rule reported PASS having never looked at it.
